novel_features.name: Cross-org patch-gap report
novel_features.description: See every device still missing or failing a patch across all your client organizations in one fleet-wide view.
novel_features.rationale: The NinjaOne console and API are organization-scoped; only a local join across synced os_patches, software_patches, devices, and organizations produces a single fleet-wide gap report.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when an agent needs the org-by-org patch posture in one shot instead of paging the per-org dashboard.

novel_features.name: Throttled cross-org patch sweep
novel_features.description: Scan and apply patches across a device cohort, serialized through an adaptive Retry-After limiter so bulk runs survive NinjaOne's throttling.
novel_features.rationale: Competing tools apply patches naively and hit 429s almost immediately on large fleets; only the local cohort plus the adaptive limiter makes a fleet-wide sweep reliable.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when an agent must remediate a cohort of devices and naive bulk apply would melt the API.

novel_features.name: Alert-storm clustering
novel_features.description: Collapse a flood of active alerts into ranked incidents grouped by organization, condition, and time window.
novel_features.rationale: Mechanical group-by over the local alert store turns 200 raw alerts into the handful of real incidents behind them; no single API call clusters alerts.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this during an alert flood to tell one site-wide incident from many unrelated alerts.

novel_features.name: Patch-stuck detector
novel_features.description: Surface KBs that have been failing or pending across multiple consecutive syncs, not just at this moment.
novel_features.rationale: Requires a local time-series of patch state retained across syncs; the API exposes no patch history.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when an agent needs the chronically-broken patches worth manual intervention, not the transient ones.

novel_features.name: Bulk alert reset by query
novel_features.description: Reset every alert matching a predicate (condition, organization, or age) in one throttled, dry-run-first operation.
novel_features.rationale: Single-alert reset exists everywhere; reset-by-cohort resolved from a local-store predicate and serialized through the limiter does not.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to clear a weekend's worth of accumulated or auto-resolved alerts without clicking each one.

novel_features.name: Stale/offline device sweep
novel_features.description: Find stale or offline devices with no contact in N days across every organization, grouped by org, with an optional throttled cohort reboot.
novel_features.rationale: A cross-org local query no org-scoped console view provides, joined with last-contact data from the synced store.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this during fleet-hygiene sweeps to find decommission candidates fleet-wide.

novel_features.name: Flapping-alert detector
novel_features.description: Rank conditions that repeatedly fire and auto-resolve over a window, by cycle count per device and condition.
novel_features.rationale: Counts fire/resolve cycles from retained local alert history; the API has no flap history to query.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to find noisy monitors worth tuning instead of resetting nightly.

novel_features.name: Custom-field hygiene
novel_features.description: Find devices and organizations missing required custom-field values (asset tag, warranty, owner) fleet-wide.
novel_features.rationale: Joins the local custom_field_definitions with per-entity custom-field values to flag SOP gaps no single API call surfaces.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when an agent must enforce documentation SOPs across the whole fleet before an audit.

narrative.headline: Every NinjaOne endpoint plus fleet-wide cross-org commands the org-scoped console can't give you.
narrative.value_prop: A complete CLI and MCP for the NinjaOne RMM API: all 300+ endpoints reachable, the high-value ones promoted to ergonomic commands, and a local SQLite store that powers offline fleet-wide search and cross-org rollups. Commands like patch-gaps, alert-storms, and stale-devices answer questions the per-organization console and API cannot, and an adaptive Retry-After limiter keeps bulk operations alive under NinjaOne's throttling.
narrative.auth_narrative: NinjaOne uses OAuth2 client-credentials. Create a Client App ID under Administration -> Apps -> API, then set NINJAONE_CLIENT_ID and NINJAONE_CLIENT_SECRET. The CLI exchanges them for a bearer token at /ws/oauth/token (scopes monitoring, management, control) and refreshes it automatically. Set NINJAONE_INSTANCE if you are not on the US region (app.ninjarmm.com).

quickstart.comment: Confirm credentials, region, and API reachability before anything else.
Pull core fleet state into the local store so offline and cross-org commands work.
See every device missing a critical patch across all organizations at once.
Collapse the active alert flood into the real incidents behind it.
Find devices gone quiet fleet-wide for a hygiene sweep.

troubleshoots.fix: Set NINJAONE_CLIENT_ID and NINJAONE_CLIENT_SECRET, then run `ninjaone-pp-cli doctor`.

troubleshoots.symptom: 403 forbidden on a write command (patch-sweep, alert-clear)
troubleshoots.fix: Your Client App ID lacks the management scope; recreate it with monitoring, management, and control.

troubleshoots.symptom: 429 Too Many Requests during a large sync or sweep
troubleshoots.fix: The adaptive limiter already honors Retry-After; lower --max-scan-pages or narrow the --df filter to reduce volume.
Run `ninjaone-pp-cli sync` first; cross-org commands read the local store.
Set NINJAONE_INSTANCE to your shard (eu.ninjarmm.com, ca.ninjarmm.com, or oc.ninjarmm.com).

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when an agent or technician needs to query, report on, or act across an entire NinjaOne fleet — especially across multiple client organizations at once. It is the right tool for patch-compliance reporting, alert-storm triage, stale-device hygiene, and any bulk device action that would otherwise require clicking through org-scoped dashboards. The local store makes fleet-wide questions cheap and keeps bulk operations from hitting rate limits.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI for live remote-control sessions or screen sharing; that is the NinjaOne console's job.
Do not use it to configure agent installers or deployment packages; use the NinjaOne web UI.
Do not use it as a real-time monitoring dashboard; it is a query/report/act tool, not a live feed beyond `tail`.
